# Third-party notices

`Sources/AU05Device/Protocol.swift` adapts report encryption/decryption, command formats and physical button identifiers from [AU05 Keys](https://github.com/elliclee/ulanzi-au05-keys), revision `7819351a5ba5c68874d0519fabe3bf62db47e328` (`Battery.swift`, `VendorKeys.swift`, `Core.swift`). Copyright (c) 2026 AU05 Keys contributors. The complete MIT license is retained in [AU05-Keys-LICENSE](AU05-Keys-LICENSE) and included in app bundles.

The native HID transport and lifecycle are implemented here. No Ulanzi proprietary binary or firmware is distributed.

The optional DualSense microphone helper bundles libopus from [Opus / Xiph.Org](https://opus-codec.org/). Its upstream [copyright and license notices](Opus-COPYING.txt) are retained here and shipped in the app resources as `Opus-COPYING.txt`. These third-party notices remain independent of the VibeWand noncommercial license.

Command mode's kernel is assembled by `scripts/build-kernel.sh` and shipped in the app under `Contents/Resources/kernel`; none of it is stored in this repository.

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24.21.0, the official Apple Silicon build, unmodified and with its original signature. Its license, which also covers the libraries built into it, ships as `kernel/node/LICENSE`.
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.2.0-rc.2 (MIT), limited to the packages VibeWand's coordinator bundle names (`kernel/coordinator/package.json`), the launcher's own support packages and, in the version after 0.9.0, its SenseVoice plug-in (`kernel/package.json`), together with the dependencies recorded in `kernel/package-lock.json`. Among those is its multi-provider model component, which builds on [pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai) (MIT) and on the SDKs of the services it can reach: OpenAI (Apache-2.0), Anthropic (MIT), Google Gen AI (Apache-2.0) and AWS (Apache-2.0).
- Installed on Apple Silicon, the kernel holds 222 packages besides VibeWand's own bundle. 79 are DeepSeek Harness's own, MIT apart from two under BSD-3-Clause. The other 143 come from third parties, under the MIT (83), Apache-2.0 (40), BSD-3-Clause (12), ISC (4), 0BSD, Python-2.0, Unlicense and LGPL-3.0-or-later (one each) licenses. Each names its license in its own `package.json` inside `kernel/node_modules`, and all but twelve also carry the license text there: nine MIT or Apache-2.0 packages published without a license file of their own, the two sherpa-onnx packages and the prebuilt libvips, both described next. An earlier wording of this notice gave 216 as the number of third-party packages; that figure counted the harness's own packages too.
- Dictation's SenseVoice service runs the recogniser of the harness's SenseVoice plug-in (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-speech-to-text-sensevoice`, MIT). The plug-in uses [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) 1.13.8 (Apache-2.0): the package `sherpa-onnx-node` and the prebuilt `sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64`, shipped unmodified under `kernel/node_modules`, about 34 MB, and loaded only while SenseVoice recognises a recording. Neither package carries a license text, so the texts are kept here and shipped in the app resources: sherpa-onnx's license as [sherpa-onnx-LICENSE](sherpa-onnx-LICENSE), and for the prebuilt package's `libonnxruntime.dylib`, which is [ONNX Runtime](https://onnxruntime.ai) 1.28.2 (MIT, Microsoft Corporation), its license as [ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE](ONNX-Runtime-LICENSE) with the notices for the libraries built into it as [ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt](ONNX-Runtime-ThirdPartyNotices.txt). The three are the files of those versions as their projects publish them. This is new since 0.9.0 and has not been released.
- The prebuilt package's `libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib` has more than sherpa-onnx built into it. sherpa-onnx's build files for 1.13.8 (the `cmake` folder of its repository) name the libraries and the revisions used, and the file that ships holds code of each: kaldi-native-fbank, kaldi-decoder, kaldifst, OpenFst and simple-sentencepiece (Apache-2.0, the license in `sherpa-onnx-LICENSE`), JSON for Modern C++ and piper-phonemize (MIT), hclust-cpp (BSD-2-Clause), Eigen (MPL-2.0, source at [libeigen/eigen](https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen)) and, for speech synthesis, [eSpeak NG](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng) in the fork `csukuangfj/espeak-ng`, under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. VibeWand only recognises speech and never calls the synthesis code, but that code is in the library as published. Before a release ships it, one of two things has to happen, and the owner has not decided which: the library ships as it is, with the GNU GPL 3.0 text, a pointer to eSpeak NG's source and the MIT and BSD notices of the others added to this folder; or the kernel takes this one library from the build sherpa-onnx publishes without speech synthesis (`sherpa-onnx-v1.13.8-osx-arm64-shared-no-tts-lib` on its release page), whose build leaves eSpeak NG and piper-phonemize out, with the MIT and BSD notices of what remains added here.
- The models SenseVoice needs are not part of the app and are not stored in this repository. When the user asks for them, VibeWand downloads the files the plug-in pins from Hugging Face or its mirror: SenseVoiceSmall as converted for sherpa-onnx (`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17`, from [FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice)) and Silero VAD (`csukuangfj/vad`, from [snakers4/silero-vad](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad)). Their terms are those published on their own pages.
- The harness's picture store (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local`), which holds a picture a tool shows the model, uses [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com) 0.35.5 (Apache-2.0) and with it the prebuilt [libvips](https://www.libvips.org) for Apple Silicon, `@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64` 1.3.4, under **LGPL-3.0-or-later**. It is one dynamic library, `kernel/node_modules/@img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64/lib/libvips-cpp.8.18.7.dylib`, shipped unmodified, loaded only when the model is shown a picture, and replaceable with a build of your own. The `README.md` beside it lists every library built into it with its license (among them glib, pango, librsvg, libheif, libexif and fribidi under the LGPL, cairo under the MPL 1.1), `versions.json` gives their versions, and the build recipes with pointers to the sources are at [lovell/sharp-libvips](https://github.com/lovell/sharp-libvips). This is new since 0.9.0 and has not been released. Before a release ships it, the texts of the GNU LGPL 3.0 and GPL 3.0 have to be added to this folder; the package itself carries neither.

VibeWand's coordinator bundle (`kernel/coordinator`, installed in the kernel as the package `vibewand-coordinator`) is part of VibeWand. The same bundle, and the overlay beside it (`kernel/overlay`), ship as `Contents/Resources/harness/` for a DeepSeek Harness the user installed themselves. In that mode nothing of the harness is shipped or modified: the user's own installation runs it.
